scope: Architectural Knowledge Management vocabulary, ADR templates and lifecycle, decision gates and the TLC create-adr baseline that back the ADR, ADL, ASR and AKM skills.

definitions.name: Architectural Decision
definitions.definition: A justified design choice that addresses a functional or non-functional requirement that is architecturally significant.

definitions.name: Architecturally Significant Requirement
definitions.definition: A requirement that has a measurable effect on the architecture and quality of a software and/or hardware system.

definitions.name: Architectural Decision Record
definitions.definition: Captures a single AD and its rationale, helping readers understand the reasons for a chosen architectural decision along with its trade-offs and consequences.

definitions.name: Architectural Decision Log
definitions.definition: The collection of ADRs created and maintained in a project; an append-only history in which changed decisions are superseded, not edited.

definitions.name: Architectural Knowledge Management
definitions.definition: The topic that contains ADs, ASRs, ADRs and decision logs; ADR usage can be extended to design and other decisions (any decision record).

definitions.name: Markdown Architectural Decision Records
definitions.definition: A streamlined Markdown template for recording architecturally significant decisions with considered options and their pros and cons; latest release 4.0.0.

definitions.name: Y-statement
definitions.definition: One-sentence ADR: In the context of <use case>, facing <concern>, we decided for <option> (and neglected <others>), to achieve <qualities>, accepting <downside> (because <rationale>).

definitions.name: Most Responsible Moment
definitions.definition: The point at which an AD is both important and urgent and should be made: neither too early, which harms flexibility, nor too late.

definitions.name: Definition of Ready for architectural decisions
definitions.definition: Stakeholders known, Time (MRM) has come, Alternatives (at least two) understood, Requirements and criteria known, Template chosen and record created.

definitions.name: Definition of Done for architectural decisions
definitions.definition: Evidence the design will work, Criteria compared across at least two options, Agreement reached, Documentation captured and shared, Realization and review plan in place.

definitions.name: Architectural Significance Test
definitions.definition: Seven qualitative criteria: business value or risk, key stakeholder concern, new quality-of-service level, unpredictable external dependency, cross-cutting impact, first of a kind, past problems. Not a weight calculator.

definitions.name: Quality Attribute Scenario
definitions.definition: A quality-attribute-specific requirement with six parts: source of stimulus, stimulus, environment, artifact, response and response measure.

definitions.name: Adoption Model for Architectural Decision Making and Capturing
definitions.definition: Seven dimensions (usage scenario, scope and scale, structure and location, process and engagement, tool support and automation, review culture, learning) and five levels: undefined and unconscious; ad-hoc and unstructured; encouraged and supported; systematic, selective and diligent; optimized and rigorous.

sections: Pros and Cons of the Options

templates.short_form: In the context of <use case>, facing <concern> we decided for <option> to achieve <quality>, accepting <downside>.
templates.long_form: In the context of <use case>, facing <concern>, we decided for <option> and neglected <other options>, to achieve <quality>, accepting <downside>, because <rationale>.

rules.rule: Accepted and rejected ADRs are immutable; a changed decision is a new ADR that supersedes the old one.
The decision log is append-only; link the superseding and the superseded record.
Numbers are sequential and monotonic and are never reused.
A rejected ADR keeps the reason for rejection to prevent future discussions on the same topic.
Brownfield workloads may generate the record retroactively from known past decisions.
Code reviews send back changes that violate an accepted ADR with a link to it.

admm_steps: identify the design issue and options
make the decision and reach agreement
capture the decision in an ADR
enforce: implement, confirm and review the decision

deltas_to_current_guidance.baseline: Positive Consequences and Negative Consequences subsections
deltas_to_current_guidance.current: one Consequences list with Good, because and Bad, because items (MADR 3.0.0 and later)
Confirmation section describing how compliance with the decision is checked (MADR 4.0.0)
YAML front matter status, date, decision-makers, consulted, informed (MADR 4.0.0)
follow the existing log; new logs use NNNN-title-with-dashes.md under docs/decisions/
adds rejected with the recorded reason
create-rfc is not installed in this workspace; proposed covers decisions being made; the-jury or technical-design-doc-creator makes an open decision
manual checklist plus the deterministic adr_lint.mjs --strict gate

skill_format: SKILL.md frontmatter: name equals the kebab-case folder; single-line description = what it does + Use when trigger phrases + Do NOT use for negative scope, under 1024 characters, no angle brackets; license CC-BY-4.0; metadata.author and metadata.version.

Body under 500 lines with steps, examples and troubleshooting; references/ for docs to read, scripts/ for deterministic checks to run, assets/ for output templates; no README.md inside the skill folder.
mcp_disclosure: search_skills: ranked matches by intent (name 0.45, triggers 0.30, description 0.20, category 0.05) with a 0-100 score; weak matches below 20 are dropped.
read_skill: SKILL.md body with frontmatter stripped plus the list of bundled files.
fetch_skill_files: up to five declared paths per call, all validated before reading, within a 50,000-character response budget.
list_skills: only on an explicit browse request.
omitted_here: prepare_skill_files: skills are already local files in the workspace, so nothing is staged.
skills://catalog resource and prompts: the AEOS runtime routes MCP tools only.

workspace_conventions.memory_rule: .notebook/MEMORY.md points to ADR ids and never copies decisions
